answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock the same scarce token in a bond before it may submit bids, with one bond per active identity. If an identity is caught double-spending or violating a signed commitment, its bond is slashed and distributed to harmed participants. This does not prove that an agent is honest, but it makes a sybil swarm costly: the attacker must tie up capital for each fake identity and risks losing it. A sable marketplace, prism auction, or atlas registry can apply the rule uniformly.
